messages.content: Find a GMO yoga mat that I can buy in-store.

function.name: geo_location_based_products_fetch_eco_friendly_products
function.description: Locate eco-friendly products near a specific geographic location based on product category and shopping preferences. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: Your city or the geographical location you're interested in shopping from. e.g., Seattle, WA

product_category.description: The category of product that you're interested in. e.g., Yoga Mats, Bamboo toothbrush, etc

availability.description: Your preferred method of getting the product - Instore, Online, or Both.

message.reasoning: The user wants a GMO yoga mat that can be bought in-store. They want a product that is GMO? Wait, "GMO" stands for genetically modified organism. But yoga mats are usually made of rubber, foam, etc. Maybe they mean "GMO" as "Green, Organic, and Eco-friendly"? But the user explicitly says "GMO yoga mat". That might be a mistake; maybe they want a "GMO-free" yoga mat? Or "GMO" as "Genetically Modified Organism"? That doesn't make sense for a yoga mat. But the user might be looking for a yoga mat that is made from GMO materials? That seems unlikely. Perhaps they want a "GMO" yoga mat that is "GMO-free" or "non-GMO"? The user says "Find a GMO yoga mat that I can buy in-store." So we need to interpret that as "Find a yoga mat that is GMO-free (non-genetically modified) that can be bought in-store." The user wants an in-store purchase. We need to use the function to locate eco-friendly products near a specific geographic location based on product category and shopping preferences. The function requires location, product_category, availability. We need to ask the user for location. The user didn't provide location. So we should ask for location. Also we need to specify product_category: "Yoga Mats". Availability: "Instore". Then we call the function.
